description: BPI-CanMV-K230D-Zero (Kendryte K230D, 128 MB LPDDR4 in package) dev board, on order. A board record: Atlas flashes it from the K230 boot ROM's USB mode with Canaan's burner U-Boot and no vendor tool; running, it serves the identity contract (board-lite, gaia/device.toml), read-only. Written from Canaan's k230_burning_tool and docs; untested on this board.

storage_target_evidence: Kendryte's CanMV K230D Zero page lists a TF card slot and no SPI-NAND or eMMC; Canaan's K230D burner defconfig enables SPI-NAND, eMMC/SD and SPI-NOR drivers without saying what the board fits.
The K230 boot ROM enters USB download mode when it can't boot from its storage (Canaan's burntool guide).
instructions: Put a blank (or erased) microSD card in the board: the boot ROM only waits for USB when it finds nothing to boot.
Connect the board's USB OTG port to this computer and power it from its other USB-C port.
The board appears as 29f1:0230 (K230 USB boot). Atlas loads Canaan's burner into it, writes the image to the card and restarts the board.
todo: Storage: the request said SPI-NAND; the board page lists only the TF slot. Check the board for a NAND part (a W25N01GW or similar); with one, storage becomes spi-nand with its geometry under flash.nand.

The burner: Gaia's K230D build (3d1f249) ships loader_mmc.bin next to sdcard.img: the SDK's U-Boot from k230d_canmv_burntool_defconfig, plain u-boot.bin with no K230 firmware head (Canaan's guide: the generated u-boot.bin is loader.bin), with USB DFU for MMC and SPI-NAND. It links at 0x80300000, so the record loads it there (k230_flash's default is 0x80360000). Gaia's sdcard.img checks out: SPL firmware heads at 1 MiB and 1.5 MiB with matching SHA-256 (Atlas checks them before every K230 flash), U-Boot at 2 MiB, env at 1.875 MiB and 3.5 MiB, boot ext4 at 30 MiB, rootfs-a at 128 MiB.

The burner's load address on the board: 0x80300000, where Gaia's burner links. k230_flash's default is 0x80360000 (kburn_k230.h:31) and its CLI accepts 0x80300000 to 0x80400000 (k230_flash.cpp:109), so 0x80300000 is in its range. Whether the boot ROM starts the burner there is UNCONFIRMED: the log's set-data-address lines show the address sent. If the boot ROM won't start it there, try 0x80360000 first.
Which of the two USB-C ports is the OTG data port, and whether a BOOT key exists (the page names a function key and a reset key only).
Whether the boot ROM wants Canaan's K230 firmware header on the burner over USB (k230_flash sends it raw).

The medium codes are settled by Canaan's k230_flash source (kburn.h:39-44): EMMC 1, SD 2, SPI-NAND 3, SPI-NOR 4 (the record's SD 2 and SPI-NAND 3 agree). Its probe (DEV_PROBE) and info replies are logged in hex on the first run.
Running, Atlas reaches it only over the network: the board has no Ethernet, and Gaia's image sets up no Wi-Fi yet, so board-lite has no address to answer on until it does.
